patch.value: Restart daily prepare when main advances before request
A queued daily release loses its day when main advances during prepare or before request. Restart fresh preparation at the current main head without retargeting verified artifacts.

Advanced main restarts complete build, verification, changelog and candidate preparation; at most two restarts; publishedToday blocks restart; repeated advance fails with the existing diagnostic; reconcile-only, retirement and recovery remain unchanged; unit and workflow contracts cover decision and counter propagation; document the same-day retry.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Root cause: prepare requires its refreshed main to equal the original trigger SHA, and request separately rejects a changed prepared base after runner queueing. Both correctly reject stale artifacts but lose the daily opportunity. Choose bounded caller workflow_dispatch (maximum two restarts), because a prepare-only loop cannot cover the separate request queue. Existing callers grant actions: write. A dedicated restart job retains read-only prepare and uses trusted workflow tools; redispatch preserves original dispatch inputs and increments prepare-restart-count. Each new run performs complete preparation at its new trigger SHA. Live GitHub publication dates block restarts after publishedToday. Scheduling counter is excluded from the durable configuration digest. Evidence: GitHub documents workflow_dispatch as a GITHUB_TOKEN recursion exception and Actions write as the dispatch endpoint permission. PR #291 is open; this work starts from main c29fe88 and is independent of its pending npm version logic.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Implementation: both existing refusal guards emit the rejected base before failing. A separate restart_prepare job runs despite failed/skipped dependencies, reads live current main and complete paginated publication dates, then redispatches the caller on main with all original workflow_dispatch inputs and counter +1. Two restarts maximum; malformed or dropped counters fail closed. Existing prepare/read and request/write permissions and recovery code are preserved. The caller template, self-pilot and migration examples now declare and forward the counter; consumer adoption requires that small caller change as well as the released workflow pin. Rejected attempts stay failed with a restart summary. Initial focused run found three old contract assumptions (only string/boolean inputs and installation in all new jobs); adjusted contracts to include numeric inputs and prove restart_prepare performs no npm installation. Typecheck, test-source typecheck and lint passed; expanded targeted regressions and changelog verification are running.

patch.value: Advanced main restarts full build, verification, changelog and candidate preparation without caller changes; at most two bot workflow_dispatch runs per caller on main per release calendar day; owner dispatches ignored; publishedToday blocks restart; history/read/pagination errors fail closed with an explicit workflow error; dispatch sends only ref main and never retirement inputs; configuration digest unchanged; reconcile-only, retirement and recovery remain unchanged; unit and workflow contracts cover history, default retirement and permissions.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Implemented input-free caller redispatch. The daily bound reads this caller workflow main-branch workflow_dispatch history since local midnight, counts triggering_actor.login with actor.login fallback only for github-actions[bot], and refuses after two bot runs. Pagination totals, duplicate identities, malformed evidence and read failures refuse with ::error::. Live publication cap remains before dispatch. Removed counter input, forwarding, documentation and digest exclusion. Fixtures cover history pages, owner actors, publication cap, DST and non-hour offsets; restart job retains contents read and actions write only.
